title: 1981-04-16_Pat_143.txt
concise_summary: PKD synthesizes his 2-3-74 mystical experience with a recent Sunday-night vision, arguing that absolute divine knowledge—not rational deduction but direct seeing as God sees—revealed the moral law as physically causal, suffering as convertible into ecstasy through agape, and Christianity as the only true solution to suffering through the incarnational logic of Christ as paradigm. He integrates this theology with his own novels (Tears, VALIS, Ubik) to argue his entire 12-year creative and personal journey was an inevitable unfolding toward mystical verification of Christian eschatological hope.
key_claims: The 2-3-74 and Sunday-night experiences were absolute knowledge (direct divine seeing), not mystical insight or satori, involving the unitary fusion of knowing and doing because God does not reason but simply is
The moral law is as real and causal as physical law; moral action has literal physical consequences, explaining karma and why Christ's vicarious atonement was necessary
Christ's conversion of suffering into ecstasy (not mere stoicism but ontological transformation) is the unique Christian miracle and superior to Buddhist liberation or Dionysian ecstasy

The true Christian exists in anticipatory ecstasy: remembering Christ's departure, awaiting his parousia (invisible return as hierogamy/union), and preparing the bridal soul for inner nuptials with God
Jesus Christ is paradigmatic (a formula), not merely historical; his life and resurrection structure all authentic Christian experience and escape from the Black Iron Prison
Agape (voluntary vicarious suffering in imitation of Christ) is the only road to penetrating suffering's ontological core and experiencing the resurrection miracle

Suffering as real and causal vs. suffering as illusion to be transcended: PKD holds both that moral law causes suffering and that Christian faith transforms it into ecstasy
